extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers, students and practitioners of astronomy/cosmology (19th-century natural philosophers)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing evidential criteria and physical arguments that support or contradict the Nebular Hypothesis for the origin of the Solar System. The text collects mechanical, dynamical, thermal, observational, and chemical lines of evidence and discusses how they should be explained by a successful cosmogony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence between inference and fact
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence between inference and fact which we find in so many planets may be held to afford strong support to the Nebular Hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hypothesis gains support where theoretical inferences (from nebular condensation processes) match observed planetary properties; broad concordance across many cases strengthens the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of revolution and rotation (synchronous rotation)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the peculiarities is the relation between the period of revolution and that of rotation: e.g., the Moon goes round its axis in the same time that it goes round the Earth; 'Against the alternative supposition, that the equality occurred by accident, the probabilities are, as Laplace says, infinity to one.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful hypothesis should provide natural physical mechanisms (Laplace's reasoning) explaining apparently purposeless synchronous relations rather than invoking design or accidental coincidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laplace resonance among satellites (mean motion relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "If the mean angular velocity of the first satellite be added to twice that of the third, the sum will be equal to three times that of the second; and from this it results that the situation of any two of them being given, that of the third can be found."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such precise arithmetic relations among satellite motions are extremely unlikely by chance and should be explicable under the nebular formation processes; their existence counts strongly for the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saturn's rings as extant witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Most significant fact of all is that presented by the rings of Saturn: they are, as it were, still extant witnesses of the genetic process he propounded. Their movements are just what, in conformity with the hypothesis, they should be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features that appear to be intermediate or persistent forms of aggregation (rings) are direct observable evidence; quantitative comparisons (e.g., rotation times 427 to 438) should match expectations from the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and formation conditions of rings
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring of a denser kind ... will be formed only near the body of a planet when it has reached so late a stage of concentration that its equatorial portions contain matters capable of easy precipitation into liquid and finally solid forms. Only where the centrifugal force has all along been very great, and remains powerful to the last, as in Saturn, can we expect dense rings to be formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hypothesis must explain why rings occur at particular distances and only under special conditions (balance of centrifugal force vs gravity, density of equatorial matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total mechanical arrangements of the Solar System
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides the most conspicuous peculiarities which first suggested the theory, there are many minor ones pointing in the same direction. Were there no other evidence, these mechanical arrangements would, considered in their totality, go far to establish the Nebular Hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should consider the ensemble of mechanical regularities (orbital inclinations, rotation rates, satellite occurrence) rather than isolated facts; cumulative agreement is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative specific gravities pattern and anomalies
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that, speaking generally, the denser planets are the nearer to the Sun, has been considered as an indication of nebular origin. But the progression of relative densities (table given) is broken and the Sun's low specific gravity is a serious objection to a simple ring-detachment explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A viable hypothesis must account for the observed pattern of planetary densities and be able to explain anomalies (e.g., Neptune denser than Saturn; Sun's low specific gravity) by invoking composition, mass, temperature, or physical state differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory causes for density anomalies
rubrics_metrics.description: Several causes may be assigned for these unlikenesses: (1) differences in elementary substances or their proportions; (2) differences in quantities of matter (mutual gravitation among molecules); (3) differences of temperatures; (4) differences of physical states (gaseous, liquid, solid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing the hypothesis against density data, explicitly consider these four factors; they serve as allowable explanatory mechanisms to reconcile theory with observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooling rate factors: surface/volume and conduction/convection
rubrics_metrics.description: In cooling of celestial bodies factors include: increase of surface vs content (surface ~ square, content ~ cube) and modes of heat escape (conduction in solids; convection in liquids/gases). Larger spheroids cool much more slowly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate theoretical cooling histories using geometric scaling and transport mechanisms; the hypothesis should predict relative cooling times consistent with observed thermal states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluid friction, rotation, and retardation of cooling
rubrics_metrics.description: In a rotating spheroid, portions of matter vary in absolute velocities; circulating currents cannot change distances from axis without loss or gain of motion. Through fluid friction force must be expended, so when a larger spheroid has higher velocity of rotation, relative slowness of circulating currents and consequent retardation of cooling are much greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess influence of rotation and fluid dynamics on thermal evolution; a correct model must include retardation of convection due to rotation and its effect on cooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation of density with size and rotation (empirical pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare great planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus) with small planets (Mars, Earth, Venus, Mercury): low density goes with great size and great velocity of rotation; high density goes with small size and small velocity. Example: Saturn vs Mercury illustrate relation with centrifugal force to gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observed correlations (size, rotation rate, density, satellite presence) as diagnostic tests of the nebular formation mechanism; success requires reproducing these group patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complicating/opposing factors in thermal evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain factors work in an opposite way and qualify effects: mutual gravitation in a large mass causes greater evolution of heat; greater velocities of circulating currents; and in the Sun, much greater central pressure leading to rapid heat genesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models must balance competing influences (slower cooling due to geometry/rotation vs faster heat generation due to mass/gravity) to explain why different bodies reached different stages of concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present and past temperature evidence (internal heat signatures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations: increasing heat below Earth's surface, volcanoes, Moon's corrugations and extinct volcanoes — these show high past/ongoing internal heat as implied by nebular condensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thermal and geological evidence should be consistent with derivation from a hot, condensed origin; a hypothesis must account for current internal heat and signs of past high temperatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical state of giant planets indicates intermediate cooling
rubrics_metrics.description: Current consensus: great planets are in stages midway between Earth and Sun. Evidence: Jupiter's central disc brightness, radiation beyond reflected sunlight, spectrum showing 'red-star line', rapid atmospheric perturbations and spots implying high internal temperature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple observational diagnostics (brightness distribution, excess radiation, spectral lines, atmospheric dynamics) to infer internal heat states and check consistency with nebular-temporal ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sun's intense incandescence explained by late formation and size
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Solar System formed by concentration of diffused matter which evolved heat, the latest-formed and largest mass will be the latest in cooling and most incandescent. The Sun's enormous mass and relatively small radiative surface explain its continued high temperature — a corollary of the Nebular Hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for the Sun's extreme thermal state by formation chronology and scaling arguments; a successful theory should make this implication natural rather than anomalous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cometary constitution and orbits as testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Most comets (omitting the periodic ones), by their physical constitution, immensely-extended and variously-directed paths, the distribution of those paths, and their manifest structural relation to the Solar System, bear testimony to the past existence of that system in a nebulous form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cometary observations (physical nature and orbital distribution) as key evidence; the hypothesis should predict and explain cometary populations and trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical evolution and the compound nature of elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The general law of evolution affords a priori grounds for suspecting the so-called elements are compounds; supporting evidence includes parallelism between allotropy and isomerism, numerous spectral lines per element, and the Newlands/Mendelejeff cyclical law. Chemical heterogeneity increases as bodies cool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether chemical diversity and observed chemical phenomena are plausibly resultant from nebular condensation and progressive chemical evolution; use geological and chemical induction to support cosmical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory sufficiency across leading phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: When we observe that by the Nebular Hypothesis the leading phenomena of the Solar System, and the heavens in general, are explicable — while current cosmogony is without a single fact to stand on — the proof becomes overwhelming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cosmogonic hypothesis should be judged by its explanatory reach: ability to account coherently for leading mechanical, thermal, chemical, and observational facts across the system lends decisive support.
